title: Mein Deutsch ist heute schlecht
desc: The kindness that makes it worse
setting: The same table, a bad night's sleep, and nine people talking at ordinary speed.

steps.speaker: Marianne
steps.es: Und was machen Sie beruflich, also genau?
steps.en: And what do you do for work, exactly?

options.es: Wie sagt man das auf Deutsch?
options.en: How do you say that in German?
options.feedback: A question, not a weakness. It is the single most useful sentence in the language.

options.es: Also. Ich mache... Zahlen und Briefe.
options.en: So. I do... numbers and letters.
options.feedback: Also buys you two seconds and everybody uses it. The answer that follows is the true one anyway.
It is. It is also the sentence that ends the conversation instead of opening it.

steps.speaker: Reto
steps.es: Soll ich es auf Englisch erklären?
steps.en: Shall I explain it in English?

options.es: Bitte nicht. Ich brauche das Deutsch.
options.en: Please do not. I need the German.
options.feedback: Say it. He means well and he does not know, and nobody will do this part for you.
It is easier and it is the wrong direction. In English you are a different person, and they will meet that one instead.
Clear and slightly cold. One more sentence saying why turns a refusal into a reason.

steps.speaker: Marianne
steps.en: I will just talk more slowly.

options.es: Sie können normal reden. Ich frage, wenn etwas fehlt.
options.en: You can talk normally. I will ask if I miss something.
options.feedback: Kind and it hands the job back to you, which is where it belongs. She will do it, too.
Sometimes it does. It also tells the table you are not keeping up, which is the part that stings.
Today you do not. Pretending puts you back in the same position in twenty minutes.
He said one word to a table of nine and it settled the matter. Nothing more is needed from you.
Fine. He did not do it as a favour, he did it because he agreed.
He closed it. Reopening it to agree with him is the one thing that could unclose it.
